subject: EdgePeak on-prem deploy — readiness & architecture questions
messages:
From: Elena Simmons <elena.simmons@edgepeak.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T10:12:00Z
Subject: EdgePeak on-prem deployment: kickoff and architecture questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we’re ready to start scoping the on-prem deployment for EdgePeak’s inference cluster. We expect this to be a multi-rack deployment in our primary datacenter (NYC). A few high-level asks to help us prepare the SOW and procurement: 

- Target throughput: ~1,200 inference QPS peak (batched), with low-latency 95th pct target of ~150ms for small text prompts.
- Expected nodes: initial phase 12 servers (GPU-capable), scale to ~36 within 9–12 months.
- Data retention: model artifacts and KV cache persistence for 30 days; PHI coverage (HIPAA) for some payloads.
- Network: we will run the cluster in a customer VPC with strict egress rules; we need guidance on NAT/egress and peering for the Redwood control plane.

Can you share a preflight checklist and a recommended node/storage architecture for our first pilot? Also please confirm whether KMS integration is required for the private control plane and any implications for firmware-level encryption (e.g., NVMe TEE).

Would be great to have a 30–45 minute technical kickoff early next week. Tom (cc’d) will be our infrastructure lead.

Thanks,
Elena Simmons
VP Infrastructure & Operations
EdgePeak Medical
elena.simmons@edgepeak.io
(212) 555-0192
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Simmons <elena.simmons@edgepeak.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgePeak on-prem deployment: kickoff and architecture questions

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the targets. We can absolutely support a private VPC/on-prem deployment with HIPAA controls; I’ve attached our preflight template to capture the site inventory and security requirements. High-level answers inline below and we’ll cover details on the call: 

- Throughput/latency: we’ll recommend a mix of GPU node sizes (A100-class or equivalent) plus CPU-only fronting pods for lightweight preprocessing. Expect to run two model-serving node pools (gpu-serving, gpu-cache) plus a small cpu-frontpool.
- Storage: we recommend encrypted block storage for model artifacts (backed by your KMS) and local NVMe on serving nodes for KV cache and hot-token storage. A cold tier (<30d) can be mounted as network blockstore (iSCSI or SAN) or object storage if your environment supports it.
- Networking: control-plane endpoints can be peered to your VPC; we’ll need a dedicated egress NAT for telemetry/updates and a firewall rule set for control-plane health checks. We’ll share a minimal set of CIDR/IPs for allowlisting.
- KMS: yes — for HIPAA we advise integrating your KMS (HSM-backed) with our private control plane. Keys never leave your environment.

Attached: EP_Preflight_Template.xlsx — please fill the site inventory and the rack-level hardware details.

Next steps: 1) schedule a 30–45m tech kickoff (Irene on our side will run the deep dive), 2) you populate the preflight sheet, 3) we produce an initial cluster topology + BOM and a short security appendix for your procurement team.

Irene/Laura — looping you in to lead the kickoff and the topology design. 

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Subject: Re: EdgePeak on-prem deployment: kickoff and architecture questions

Thanks Karthik — attaching a filled site inventory CSV with rack power, switch top-of-rack details, and expected network VLANs. Quick clarifications: 

- We have 5 racks reserved in the pilot cage. Planned per-rack: 3 GPU servers (dual-socket + 8x NVMe) and 1 management server.
- Storage: SAN present (iSCSI) but ops prefers local NVMe for hot cache; long-term model store will be on the SAN-backed block store.
- KMS: we run Vault HSM-backed keys; procurement will provide an endpoint for KMS integration.
- Compliance: our security team will require an audit log export for all user-level API calls for 90 days.

Questions: 1) will Redwood’s runtime persist KV cache across node restarts if local NVMe fails or should we rely on a network-backed replication? 2) recommended PV sizing strategy for model downloads vs ephemeral workspaces?

Attachment: edgepeak-site-inventory.csv

- Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:10:00Z
Subject: Internal: EdgePeak pilot — topology, node pools & storage decisions (action items)

Team — quick internal summary after Elena’s site inventory. I captured the constraints and our recommended starting architecture. Please review and call out any gaps before the kickoff at 2027-03-03T15:00Z (PT).

Summary of constraints from customer:
- 5 racks, pilot = 12 GPU servers (3 per rack in planned layout), SAN available but ops prefers local NVMe for hot cache.
- Vault HSM KMS available for key management.
- Need 90-day API call audit logs exported to their SIEM.

Our recommended starting topology (v1):
- Control plane: private control plane components running in their VPC (control-plane endpoints peered). Minimal external egress required for telemetry; use allowlisted IPs.
- Node pools: 
  * gpu-serving (A100/80GB equiv) — 8 nodes to start; config for continuous batching, large KV locals.
  * gpu-cache (GPU + local NVMe) — 4 nodes focused on KV persistence & cold-warm migration logic.
  * cpu-frontpool — 2 x 16vCPU nodes for tokenization, input validation, and rate-limited pre-processing.
- Storage: 
  * Model artifacts (persistent): encrypted blockstore on SAN. Use LUKS + customer KMS for root encryption if they require.
  * Hot KV cache: local NVMe with periodic snapshot to SAN (every 30–60 min) for recovery. We will not rely solely on local NVMe for durability.
  * Ephemeral workspaces: ephemeral PVs on node-local or dynamic CSI with short TTL (7–14d).
- Networking: Peered VPC for control plane; require dedicated NAT egress for telemetry. Provide list of IPs and TLS cert expectations.
- Compliance/ops: enable request-level audit logging; we will produce an export connector to their SIEM (S3 or syslog) — need ops confirmation on retention and endpoint.

Action items (owners):
- Irene: prepare a short topology diagram + CIDR/IPs we'll require, and minimal firewall rules for allowlisting. (Due: 2027-03-03T12:00:00Z)
- Jonas: recommend PV classes and snapshot cadence: propose configuration for local NVMe snapshots to SAN + CSI driver options. (Due: 2027-03-03T12:00:00Z)
- Monica: confirm KMS integration steps and produce an HSM checklist (what we need from EdgePeak). (Due: 2027-03-03T12:00:00Z)
- Laura: draft a short security appendix for procurement describing audit log export, key controls, and SLA expectations. (Due: 2027-03-03T12:00:00Z)

Attached: ep_cluster_recommendations_v1.pdf (internal draft).

Notes on durability: we should not promise full KV durability from local NVMe alone — propose a hybrid approach where we accept degraded performance for short windows but guarantee recovery from SAN snapshots.

If there are no objections I’ll send this short plan to Elena ahead of the kickoff.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
